scenes.heading: Body systems working together
scenes.sub: Climbing the stairs takes four systems at once
scenes.say: Your body is made of trillions of cells, but they don't work alone. Even climbing the stairs needs your digestive, circulatory, respiratory and excretory systems all working at once.

scenes.heading: Levels of organisation
scenes.say: Remember: Cool Teens Often Sing Out. Cell, tissue, organ, system, organism. A tissue is a group of similar cells doing one job. An organ, like the stomach, is made of several different tissues. A system is a group of organs.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A depot sends trucks along freeways, side streets and return roads
scenes.science: The heart pumps blood through arteries, capillaries and veins
scenes.breaks: traffic can go both ways, but blood flows one way only, kept that way by the heart and valves. In capillaries, substances diffuse.
scenes.say: The circulatory system is like a delivery network. The heart is the depot. Arteries are freeways carrying blood away at high pressure. Capillaries are side streets reaching every door, with walls one cell thick. Veins are the return roads, with valves to stop backflow.

scenes.heading: Digestion
points: Lipase: fats into fatty acids and glycerol
Villi in the small intestine absorb nutrients
scenes.say: Digestion breaks big food molecules into small ones. Chewing and churning are mechanical. Then enzymes take over: amylase turns starch into glucose, protease turns protein into amino acids, and lipase turns fats into fatty acids and glycerol. Villi in the small intestine absorb the nutrients.

scenes.heading: Breathing vs respiration

left.title: Breathing
points: Driven by the diaphragm and ribs

scenes.say: Don't mix up breathing and respiration. Breathing moves air in and out, and gases diffuse across the alveoli. Cellular respiration is the reaction in mitochondria: glucose plus oxygen gives carbon dioxide plus water, releasing energy.
scenes.caption: Don't mix up breathing and respiration. Breathing moves air in and out, and gases diffuse across the alveoli. Cellular respiration is the reaction in mitochondria: glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water, releasing energy.

scenes.heading: Excretion
points: Removes wastes from the body's own reactions
Kidneys remove urea, extra water and salts
Removing faeces is egestion, not excretion
scenes.say: Excretion removes wastes made by your body's own reactions. The lungs excrete carbon dioxide. The kidneys filter the blood and remove urea, extra water and salts. Getting rid of faeces is called egestion, because that food was never made by your cells.

scenes.heading: Exercise data
scenes.question: Breathing rate goes from 14 to 32 breaths per minute, and heart rate from 70 to 150 beats per minute, after running. Why?
lines: They need more oxygen, make more CO₂
Breathing rises: more O₂ in, CO₂ out
scenes.say: After running, breathing rate rises from fourteen to thirty-two, and heart rate from seventy to one hundred and fifty. Muscle cells are doing more respiration, so they need more oxygen and make more carbon dioxide. Faster breathing and a faster heart deliver it all quicker.

points: Arteries go away from the heart
Gas exchange happens in the alveoli
scenes.say: Quick recap. Cells build tissues, organs and systems. Villi absorb nutrients, blood carries them, the alveoli exchange gases, and the kidneys remove urea. Every system depends on the others. Now try the practice questions!
